calibration.reference_10: Seeing Theory (Brown University) — the Sampling and Correlation chapters, the interactive explainers the field points to for teaching exactly these three ideas.
calibration.reference_8: Khan Academy's 'Correlation and causality' exercise set with BBC Bitesize KS4 scatter-graph topic: assignable as-is tomorrow, but exercise-set depth rather than simulation.

verdict: Every number I could check is true to the bundled data — population 7.30 h / 25.2% late / 57.4% at the library door, framing gap 1.8 points = 1.8% to 45% of axis height, r 0.81 falling to 0.26/0.10/0.31 within seasons — and both round-3 items are fixed. All three activities are genuine gated experiments with misconception-naming feedback, scaffolding hints, unlimited retry and explicit nuance, and free text is never fake-graded. It clears the 8 bar but not 9: one hint still hands over its answer, and the common cause is a toggle plus numbers rather than a manipulable model.

carry_over.evidence: EDUCATOR_GUIDE.md:28 now reads 'convenience draws land near the library-door share of 57.4% late-library users (against the true 25.2%) with a mean sleep about 0.4 h below the population's 7.30 h at every size — 300 seeded draws at n = 500 run roughly 53–63% late-library and 0.30–0.49 h low, while n = 10 draws scatter widely (about 10–90% late-library; means from about 0.8 h above to 1.3 h below the truth)'. I re-ran the bundled sampler 300 draws per size: convenience means 6.89 h at n = 50/200/500 (0.41 h low, i.e. 'about 0.4'), n = 500 pct 53.0–62.7 and mean 6.81–7.00 (0.30–0.49 low), n = 10 pct 10–90 and means 6.00–8.07 (0.77 above, 1.30 below). Every quoted range matches the data.

model.js:115–117 now strips negated prove/definitely/certainly before testing and only flags always/never immediately before causes/leads to; 'correlation never proves a cause' is no longer flagged. A narrow residual ('doesn't definitely prove' still strips to 'prove') is recorded under non_blocking rather than re-blocked.

non_blocking.issue: The negation strip in reviewConclusion still misses a negation separated from 'prove' by an adverb: 'does not definitely prove' / 'doesn't definitely prove' strips 'does not definitely' and leaves 'prove', so the exact cautious phrasing the lesson teaches can still be told it over-claims.

Activity 1's hint gives away the whole tick-list answer ('The first three tiles are properties of the data — they stay identical whatever the axis'), leaving only transcription; it also says 'first three' where the statistics box has four tiles, three of which are data properties.
non_blocking.fix: Replace the hint paragraph's text with: "Try the 0–100 and 70–74 presets and watch the statistics box: some of its numbers move with the axis and some never do. Work out which, then tick the matching boxes — you can check as often as you like."

non_blocking.issue: The learner screen never says why standing at the library door over-samples late-library students (every late user plus 1/4 of everyone else), so the mechanism behind the bias is only inferable from the % late-library column — the guide explains it, the learner never sees it.
non_blocking.fix: Append one sentence to the a2 hint string: "Standing at the library door at 21:00, you meet late-library students about four times as often as everyone else — ask what that does to the group you are measuring."

non_blocking.issue: The start screen promises 'the same numbers, two charts, two very different impressions', but activity 1 is one chart with two axis framings; a literal 15-year-old looks for a second chart that never appears.
non_blocking.fix: Replace that list item with: "1 · Graph framing — the same numbers, two axis framings, two very different impressions."

non_blocking.issue: The chart tables (the required non-visual alternative) start hidden and are never visible in this round's captured evidence for a1/a3, so the screenshots cannot show the alternative exists; the toggles are keyboard-operable, so this is discoverability, not a functional break.

keep: Activity 1's statistics box: three statistics that provably never move (means 72.5 / 71.4, final difference 1.8 points) beside the single number that does ('gap as drawn', 1.8 % → 45 % of axis height), with the axis controls hard-clamped (model.js AXIS_MIN_MAX / AXIS_MAX_MIN) so no data point can leave the chart.

The three misconception-specific wrong-answer branches: A1's 'any non-zero axis is deceptive' gets the hospital temperature chart; A2's 'bigger samples are noisier' gets corrected with the learner's own random draws; A3's 'just noise' is told the association is real but unexplained.

A3's correct-answer feedback: affirms the association is real (r = 0.81), shows the within-season collapse (0.26 / 0.10 / 0.31), then states what evidence would support a cause — nuance without nihilism.

The case-file review's honesty: it checks structure and wording only and says so in the feedback, and its evidence nudge quotes a concrete example ('within each season r fell to about 0.2') rather than pretending to grade prose.

The educator guide's limitations section: synthetic data disclosed, population-known-because-generated explained, residual within-season correlations (14–20 weeks per season) flagged as a stretch discussion, and 'not evaluated for learning gains' stated plainly.
gap_to_10: Seeing Theory's Sampling and Correlation chapters: the learner manipulates the model itself — dragging points and watching r redraw, drawing samples and watching the sampling distribution and interval update — so the mechanism is animated rather than toggled. Here the 52 weeks and 1,200 students are frozen, the common cause can only be revealed by colouring plus a number, and the craft (clean but single-note chart system) is not Ciechanowski-memorable.
